summary: Reviewed 7 files across 2 new credential routes (PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential, GET /api/repositories/:id/credential-options), the RepositoryManager, git-credentials utilities, requestUtils, staticServer, and the config credential endpoints. 0 Critical, 0 High, 1 Medium (host/credential coherence, documented as known), 2 Low/Info items. comments.note: MEDIUM — A04 (Insecure Design) / Trust Boundary: src/git/git-credentials.ts L104–111 (resolveCredential). The function's own JSDoc documents a known host/credential coherence gap: when credentialId is explicitly supplied, resolution performs an exact ID match with no cross-validation against the URL's hostname. This means a caller could (inadvertently or with elevated access) associate credential A (configured for host-a.example.com) with a repository whose URL resolves to host-b.example.com, and the token for host-a would be injected into requests to host-b. The API layer (PUT /credential) correctly validates that the referenced credentialId exists in appConfig.gitCredentials, but does NOT verify that credential.host matches the repository's URL host before allowing the association. Impact is limited to the local tool context (no remote attacker path under normal localhost binding), but the mismatch could cause an access token to be sent to an unintended host during git operations. Recommendation: In the PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential handler (repositories.ts L270–281), after confirming the credential exists, additionally assert that credential.host === extractHost(repo.Url) and return 400 if there is a mismatch, or at minimum surface a warning. The resolveCredential call sites in the orchestrators should also assert host coherence before injecting tokens.

LOW — A09 (Security Logging & Monitoring Failures): Neither PUT /api/repositories/:id/credential nor GET /api/repositories/:id/credential-options emit any structured audit log entries when a credential association is written or when credential options are retrieved. Given these are security-sensitive operations (associating a PAT with a repository), a structured log entry (repoId, credentialId, timestamp, action) would assist in anomaly detection and incident response. This is a defence-in-depth improvement and does not block approval given the tool's localhost-only threat model.

INFO — A01 (Broken Access Control): The server binds exclusively to 127.0.0.1 (src/server/index.ts L180: server.listen(port, '127.0.0.1', ...)), which is the correct posture for a local developer tool. No network-exposed attack surface exists for the credential routes under normal operation. This is noted as a positive control.

INFO — A02 (Cryptographic Failures / Token Masking): GET /api/repositories/:id/credential-options masks tokens with a flat '***' replacement (repositories.ts L332–334). The config endpoint (config.ts L28–30) uses a more informative 'maskToken' that reveals the last 4 characters. The difference in masking strategies between the two endpoints is an inconsistency but not a vulnerability — in the credential-options context, exposing the last 4 chars is unnecessary since the endpoint is only used to select which credential to associate. No action required.

INFO — A03 (Injection): Token injection into git URLs is performed exclusively via WHATWG URL property assignment (parsed.username = token), never via string concatenation (git-credentials.ts L150–158). This correctly prevents URL injection for all token values, including those containing '@', '/', '#', or other special characters. Positive control confirmed.

INFO — A01 (Path Traversal / Static Server): serveStatic() decodes percent-encoding before resolving the path and guards that the resolved absolute path starts with baseDir + sep (staticServer.ts L53–75). This correctly prevents %2e%2e path traversal. The X-Content-Type-Options and X-Frame-Options headers are set on all static responses, and a strict CSP (default-src 'self') is applied to HTML responses. Positive controls confirmed.

INFO — A03 (DoS / Body Size): parseJsonBody enforces a 1 MB body limit and destroys the stream on overflow (requestUtils.ts L3, L26–34). Both new credential routes parse request bodies through this guard. Positive control confirmed.
